title: Preventing XSS: reflected, stored and DOM-based

videos.script: Lucia writes to the clinic that her knee is much better. She copied the text from an e-mail, and the word much came with bold tags around it. {{bold}} In the staff inbox, the word much is bold. {{inbox}} That looks harmless. It is not. It means the inbox turned her text into markup. Any markup she sends, the browser of every receptionist will build. {{markup}} That is cross-site scripting, and it comes in three forms. The text arrives in the same request. Or it was stored earlier. Or the page's own JavaScript writes it in. {{forms}} The fix is lesson 4's, applied in the right place each time: the text stays text. {{fix}} Today you count bold elements in a real browser, and bring them to zero. {{today}}
